decisions.reason: Fixing password-dependent legacy field controls does not change the independent requirement that interactive fields have persistent help labels.
The source decision addresses the suitability of legacy field controls, but it does not change the required placeholder-clearing behavior when a field is activated.
The table-layout requirement concerns pasted table structures and page margins, not password-dependent editable field controls.
The reference to legacy fields describes an old form-control mechanism, not the separate workflow for copying content from legacy templates into new templates.
Fixing password-dependent form fields does not alter the requirement for reliable manual line breaks after pasted content.
The source decision does not discuss or alter bullet sizing, alignment, color, scaling, or visual design.
Repairing the legacy editable-field mechanism does not necessarily change the required style source, style additions, or cross-template style coverage.
The source decision concerns editable field controls and does not change Tab-driven list hierarchy or nested-list alignment.
The request to fix a discovered field-control problem does not revise the assessment task's steps, outputs, coverage, method, or time budget.
The source decision does not change the requirement to include the existing templates' theme colors in the new style system.
